facts: The hero tagline says ocx turns any OCI registry into a cross-platform binary distribution platform with zero extra infrastructure. [L8]
The hero actions link to Get Started, Install and User Guide pages. [L10]
The OCI-Native feature says a Docker Hub, GHCR, ECR or Harbor registry serves as the package server. [L23]
The Cross-Platform feature says one identifier resolves to the right binary on Linux, macOS, Windows or FreeBSD. [L28]
The Reproducible feature says a local index snapshot locks every resolution and gives the same result offline. [L33]
The Automation-First feature says ocx has JSON output, clean environments and composable commands for CI. [L38]
The Shell install command pipes a setup script from setup.ocx.sh into sh. [L52]
Install commands are provided for PowerShell, Nushell, fish and Elvish as well as the POSIX shell. [L53]
The installation page holds pinned versions, manual downloads and CI setup. [L68]
Opening a new terminal and running ocx --remote --global add uv:0.10 installs the first package. [L70]
The VS Code extension is available from the VS Marketplace and from Open VSX. [L81]
The GitHub Action setup-ocx installs ocx, pulls the project toolchain and exports its environment in one step. [L82]
ocx direnv init writes an envrc so direnv activates the project toolchain on cd. [L83]
Packages install straight from any OCI registry, with no taps, no formulas and no Artifactory. [L97]
One command installs and activates a package, and every install is content-addressed by SHA-256 digest. [L99]
OCI multi-platform manifests resolve the right build for the OS and architecture, with no mapping tables. [L109]
The same ocx add astral-sh uv command works on macOS, Linux CI runners and Windows machines. [L111]
ocx package exec layers package variables over the shell, and with --clean it strips everything else. [L121]
Passing --clean gives a hermetic scope, which suits CI pipelines and build systems. [L123]
Two tags resolving to the same build share one directory on disk, so storage scales with distinct builds. [L133]
Pinning a package to a digest gives a lockfile-free guarantee with no registry or index lookups. [L135]
Every command returns structured JSON with --format json, and there is no interactive prompt. [L145]
ocx package env prints variables for build systems, and ocx env --ci writes CI runtime files directly. [L147]
Every install is a self-contained directory, so the store can be copied to a USB drive or CI cache. [L157]
The local index snapshot and object store are all ocx --offline needs to run a bundled toolchain. [L159]
The roadmap card links to what is being built next. [L174]
The package catalog card links to index.ocx.sh for browsing public packages. [L181]
The Discord card links to the community server for questions and feedback. [L188]
The GitHub card links to the ocx repository for starring, issues and contributions. [L195]
The closing line states ocx is free to use, fork and extend. [L205]
Feature card icons are tinted with CSS filter chains, with separate dark mode variants. [L209]
The quick-start header is centred while its body is left aligned, with wider padding at 640px and 960px. [L250]
Quick-start body padding grows at the 640px and 960px breakpoints. [L278]
The CTA cards form a four-column grid, which drops to two columns at 768px and one at 480px. [L354]
Feature section images are capped at 240px wide and scale to their container. [L477]
